svg.aria-label: Flow of a go build with -toolexec in Go 1.27.2. Step 1: the go command runs the wrapper with the tool path and -V=full and uses the printed line as the tool ID. Step 2: the action ID hashes the tool ID, flags, sources and dependency IDs; the wrapper itself is not part of it. Step 3: look up the action ID in GOCACHE; on a hit the cached archive is reused and its output replayed, and the wrapper never runs for that package. Step 4: on a miss the go command runs the wrapper with the real tool path and arguments and TOOLEXEC_IMPORTPATH set; the wrapper may add or rewrite Go files and then runs the real tool. Step 5: the result is stored under the action ID. Two rules: a wrapper that prints the same -V=full line as a plain build shares cache keys with it, so append a version marker; and imports added by injected code must already be in the build graph, because importcfg lists only planned dependencies.
svg.text: go build -toolexec: where a wrapper sits, and how the build cache sees it
Go 1.27.2 cmd/go · the cache key is built from the tool ID, which is whatever "tool -V=full" prints through the wrapper

2. action ID = hash(tool ID, flags,
sources, deps' IDs) — wrapper not in it
3. look up action ID in GOCACHE
hit
cache hit: reuse archive + replay output
the wrapper never runs for this package
miss
4. run: wrapper /path/compile args…
TOOLEXEC_IMPORTPATH=example.com/app
wrapper may add or rewrite .go files,
then exec the real tool with new args
5. store result under the action ID
Two rules every rewriting wrapper needs
1. same -V=full line as a plain build => same cache keys,
so plain and instrumented archives get mixed up.
Fix: append your version (+ config hash) to the line.
2. imports added by injected code must already be in
the build graph: importcfg lists only planned deps.
stdin/stdout/stderr pass through;
exit status must be the tool's;
compile, asm, link, vet, cgo, cover…
